title: Wrong port with the real cause outside the provided context
presentedFailure: AssertionFailedError: expected <ROTTERDAM> but was <HAMBURG>. The stack trace cites only the test frame, there is no log output and no documentation is mapped. PortRouter.java is not retrieved.
knownRootCause: PortRouter.portFor only routes German cargo through Rotterdam when the system property 'export.eu.routing' is true; otherwise it returns HAMBURG. The test JVM does not set that property, so the default branch runs. The cause is a missing feature flag/configuration in the test run (or a test that does not set the flag). It cannot be established from the retrieved context.
expectedEvidence: Only the assertion message and the one-line test are available: expected ROTTERDAM, got HAMBURG for 'DE'.
There is no stack frame into PortRouter, no log and no document.
A good diagnosis can name PortRouter/routing as the component and propose hypotheses, but must say the implementation was not provided and keep confidence below HIGH.

expectedLimitationsContain: No execution log output was available
No spec or ADR is mapped to com.acme.export.routing.PortRouterTest
retrieval.answerability: NOT answerable with certainty by design: the production class that decides the port is not in the context. The correct behaviour is an honest LOW/MEDIUM diagnosis that declares the gap.

manualChecks: The diagnosis does not assert as fact a cause it could not see (for example 'the flag is not set') without marking it as a hypothesis.
The limitations say that the implementation of PortRouter and the test configuration were not provided.
